subject.title: [Bug] Docker sandbox container name collision across multiple instances on same host

question: Should OpenClaw scope non-shared sandbox runtime identity by resolved workspace root and accept the one-time old-runtime reset or cleanup behavior for existing Docker, browser, SSH, and skills workspace sandboxes?
rationale: The source-backed bug is clear, but the permanent key shape and upgrade behavior define a sandbox security boundary and affect persisted runtime reuse.

options.title: Scope by workspace and document cleanup
options.body: Proceed with the active workspace-scoping direction and require tests plus release-note or Doctor guidance for old non-shared containers and workspaces.

options.title: Require an upgrade migration
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a doctor or migration path before merge if preserving old non-shared runtime state matters.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle design
options.body: Pause the narrow fix if maintainers want the broader sandbox lifecycle issue to define one combined identity and cleanup contract first.

recommendation.title: Scope by workspace and document cleanup
recommendation.body: Proceed with the active workspace-scoping direction and require tests plus release-note or Doctor guidance for old non-shared containers and workspaces.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sandbox security/product history in the inspected git history and is tied to adjacent lifecycle direction.
